for testing that software reproduces what it prints. source: the citation. experiments: none (the paper has

standard response surface designs of its Table 1, and its catalogue of enumerated designs; expected: every number

a quotation) and check: design_metric (evaluate_design on the runs, or on a design generate_design makes) or

when there is one; disagreement says why a printed number does not reproduce. not_captured: what is left out.

designs.notes: The paper's ME, ME+IE and SOE models are the library's main_effects, interactions and quadratic. Prediction variance pv is f(x)'(X'X)^-1 f(x) over the cube [-1, 1]^5; evaluate_design samples 100,000 uniform points (seed 42) and adds the cube's vertices for the maximum. The Int. row of Table 6 tests a main effect in the model of the intercept and that main effect, and its last two rows test one interaction or one quadratic effect added to the main-effects model (after Jones and Nachtsheim 2011a); every interaction (and every quadratic effect) of Design 1 gives the same power there, so X1:X2 and X1^2 stand for all. The minimum power over the interactions in the ME+IE model is read as the minimum over all its terms, since the main effects' power is higher. Table 7's qq,ss correlations are all 1/12, so one entry of the matrix stands for them; the largest correlation of any type is the qq,st maximum, 0.553, as the table itself shows; another minimum or maximum is read from a pair of terms attaining it. A minimum or maximum of Tables 10 and 11 is checked on the projection attaining it, found by evaluating every projection with evaluate_design; an average is manual.
